clue.text: One stops peaceniks before fully mounting show

indicators.note: one piece stops up, or plugs, the gap inside another

parts.note: CND, the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament, a British peace movement
one is the Roman numeral I
ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting means the word rises, so it is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: fully means all, completely

explanation.surface: A lone figure holds up peace campaigners just before a show is staged in full.
explanation.walkthrough: CND is the British Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament. 'Mounting' turns ALL upwards to LLA, which goes at the foot of this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The theme is pantomime, and this rags-to-riches tale is one of the best-loved Christmas shows.

clue.text: Dismiss Penthouse centrefold that's wasted

indicators.note: a centrefold is the middle pages of a magazine, so the letters come from the middle of these words

explanation.surface: Getting rid of the men's magazine's centre spread is money thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centrefold' looks like the magazine's pin-up, but it tells you to take the letters from the middle of 'Dismiss Penthouse'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe time or money squandered, used to no good purpose, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Show person former airline task bar first

parts.note: BEA was British European Airways, merged into British Airways in 1974

indicators.note: bar means except, so the task word is taken without its first letter

parts.note: a duty is a task you must do

explanation.surface: A performer from an old airline is assigned a job, the bar coming first.
explanation.walkthrough: BEA, British European Airways, is a defunct UK airline. 'Bar first' means except the first letter, so DUTY loses its D.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of the pantomime and fairy tale with the Beast is a character in a seasonal show.

clue.text: Show person unfinished racket

indicators.note: unfinished means the final letter of the word for racket is left off

parts.note: babel is a confused din, a racket of noise

explanation.surface: A performer with a racket that is still being made.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the Babes in the Wood, a traditional British pantomime, is a stage character.

clue.text: Rutter orchestrated things for prenuptial dos

parts.note: a male deer in the rutting season, a stag, is one that ruts

indicators.note: orchestrated means arranged, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: John Rutter, the composer, scored some pieces for wedding-eve parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rutter' looks like the composer's name but means a rutting animal. 'Orchestrated' rearranges THINGS into NIGHTS.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the parties held for a groom before his wedding, so they are dos before the nuptials.

clue.text: Gym painter decorated, ignoring current show

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym

indicators.note: decorated suggests the letters are done up again in a fresh pattern
ignoring means the letter for current is left out of the word

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: The school gym has been redecorated by a painter, ignoring the current exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' is the electrical symbol I, not the present exhibition; 'ignoring' drops it, and 'decorated' shuffles what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: The play about the boy who never grows up is a regular Christmas pantomime show.

clue.text: Show person one Zulu in charge

indicators.note: in says these letters are set inside the word for charge

parts.note: a ward is someone in your charge
one is the Roman numeral I
Zulu is the NATO alphabet word for Z

explanation.surface: A performer, a single Zulu man in command.
explanation.definitionFit: The magician of Oz is a character in the stage show, as in pantomime versions of that story.

clue.text: Show person mature under pressure

indicators.note: in a down clue the word placed under another comes after it

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure in physics
to mature is to age

explanation.surface: A performer grows up under stress.
explanation.definitionFit: A young attendant, like the boy servant in many pantomimes, is a stock stage character.

clue.text: One can rave about English Rover

indicators.note: about here sets the rave beside English, the rant following it

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a tin is a can
to rant is to rave

explanation.surface: Someone could rant about the English, from a wandering perspective.
explanation.definitionFit: A rover is someone who wanders from place to place, a travelling person without a fixed home.

clue.text: She showed some initiative after revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so the letters are read backwards
some says only part of the word is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: A woman showed some enterprise after a political uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes ATIVE from the end of 'initiative', and 'after revolution' turns it around. The definition is cryptic: a musical named after a woman, so a show that is a she.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lloyd Webber musical about Eva Peron is a female title role that was put on stage.

clue.text: Duke is placed next to earl in row

indicators.note: next to sets the earl alongside the preceding letters

parts.note: to put something is to place it

explanation.surface: A duke is seated beside an earl in a line of nobles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' rhymes with cow here, a quarrel, not a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A row, pronounced like cow, is a noisy quarrel or argument, a synonym.

clue.text: Cook agreed to keep new pineapple

indicators.note: to keep means the outer letters hold the new letter inside them
to cook is to mix up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chef consents to store a fresh pineapple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pineapple' is old military slang for a hand bomb, from its ridged casing; it is not the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Pineapple is slang for a hand-thrown bomb, from the segmented shape of the old Mills bomb.

clue.text: Mike abandons correct piping

indicators.note: abandons means the letter for Mike walks out of the word for correct

parts.note: to remedy a fault is to correct it
Mike is the NATO alphabet word for M

explanation.surface: Mike leaves the plumbing work set right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Correct' is a verb here, giving REMEDY; 'piping' is the adjective for a thin high voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A piping voice is thin and high-pitched, and a reedy voice is likewise shrill and thin.

clue.text: Galvanised party with joint exercises first

indicators.note: first says the preceding pieces come before the party

parts.note: the hip is a joint of the body
PE, physical education, means exercises
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A political party fired up by doing joint exercises before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party. 'First' puts W, HIP and PE ahead of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To galvanise people is to rouse them to action, and to stir them up means the same.

clue.text: Bush left in more spacious cape

indicators.note: in places the letter for left inside the word for more spacious

parts.note: wider means more spacious
a ness is a headland or cape, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: A shrub planted on the left of a broader headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' is the wild back country, as in Australia, not a shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: The bush is wild uncultivated country far from towns, a synonym for untamed land.

clue.text: People of power head south, drinking old red wine

indicators.note: drinking means the outer letters take in the others, swallowing them

parts.note: the pate is the top of the head
tent is a deep red Spanish wine, used for communion

explanation.surface: Powerful people go south and drink old red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Tent is an old name for a dark red Spanish wine, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Despots, monarchs and rulers wielding great authority are mighty figures holding sway.

clue.text: Relax and laugh a little, not hysterically

indicators.note: hysterically suggests wild disorder, so these letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Calm down and have a gentle chuckle, but not a fit of giggles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hysterically' rearranges the letters of LAUGH A LITTLE NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to stop holding back and behave in a relaxed, uninhibited way.

clue.text: Show person area in ancient city above Troy

indicators.note: in a down clue, above puts the city before the troy letter
in places the area letter inside the name of the ancient city

parts.note: Thebes was an ancient city of Egypt and of Greece
t is an abbreviation for troy, the system of weights

explanation.surface: A performer in an old city, sited above Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troy' looks like the ancient city beside Thebes but is troy weight, abbreviated T.
explanation.definitionFit: The monster who loves Beauty is a character in the fairy-tale pantomime.

clue.text: Histrionic 8 inducted into bizarre erotica

indicators.note: inducted into means taken inside, so the letter goes within the others
bizarre suggests strange disorder, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to clue 8 is abbreviated P, as in p. for a numbered sheet of a book

explanation.surface: A melodramatic youth is drawn into strange erotica.
explanation.walkthrough: '8' refers to the answer of 8-down, whose standard abbreviation is P.
explanation.definitionFit: Histrionic behaviour is overdramatic, as exaggerated as an opera singer's performance.

clue.text: Poles used to be right among Anglo-Saxon respondents

indicators.note: among says these letters sit inside the abbreviation

parts.note: N and S are the north and south poles
were means used to be

explanation.surface: Poles were properly counted among the Anglo-Saxon people who replied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like the nationality but means the magnetic poles N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: People who reply to questions are respondents, and the agent noun names the same people.

clue.text: Show person's choice of rides in Badminton

indicators.note: choice of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A performer's pick of horse rides at the Badminton trials.
explanation.walkthrough: Badminton is the English horse trials, not the racket sport. The definition's 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The sailor of the Arabian Nights is the hero of a traditional pantomime, a stage character.

clue.text: Show place, extremely old dilapidated one

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremities, the first and last letters of the word
dilapidated means falling apart, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A theatre, extremely old and falling into ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a well-known British chain of cinemas, a place where films are shown.

clue.text: Simpson is back initially with a Native American

parts.note: O. J. Simpson, the American footballer, is known by his initials OJ

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: Simpson is back at first with a Native American.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a people of the Great Lakes region, also called Chippewa, a First Nations group.

clue.text: Horse has gone off to get cooler

parts.note: a dun is a horse of greyish-brown colour

indicators.note: off means gone bad or awry, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: The horse has gone off to get a little cooler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooler' is slang for a prison cell, not something colder.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooler is slang for a jail cell, and a dark underground cell is a prison.

clue.text: Show person, lawyer and writer

parts.note: a DA is a district attorney, a US prosecuting lawyer
the writer of the clue refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: A performer, a lawyer and an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' is the setter, who refers to themselves as ME.
explanation.definitionFit: The pantomime woman played by a man in drag is the stock comic figure of the show.

clue.text: Briefly excuse sailor with a show person

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: an alibi is an excuse
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A short excuse from a sailor with a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: The woodcutter of the forty thieves tale is the hero of a traditional pantomime.

clue.text: Like child at show, past caring at the end

parts.note: ago means in the past

indicators.note: at the end means only the final letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: Like a child at a performance, having stopped caring by the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A child at a pantomime is eager and excited, wide-eyed with anticipation.

clue.text: Ditches old bird on way back

parts.note: the moa is an extinct flightless bird of New Zealand

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: An old bird abandons someone on the way home.
explanation.definitionFit: Water-filled trenches around castles are protective channels dug into the ground.

clue.text: Show person in show with wet pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are rearranged badly

explanation.surface: A performer in a show wets their trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like trousers, but it is British slang for rubbish, an anagram signal on IN SHOW and WET.
explanation.definitionFit: The princess of the seven dwarfs story is the heroine of a popular pantomime.
